Baghdad is retaken, and Palestine is held more thinly to pay for it. What actually happened: Baghdad fell to the British on 11 March 1917, and the Yildirim army group, formed in 1917 under German command, was sent to Palestine and not to Mesopotamia. Jerusalem fell on 9 December 1917, and the British entered Damascus on 1 October 1918. The Yildirim army group was a German project that failed to retake Baghdad because it was sent to Palestine and was too weak when it got there, and the British advanced on both fronts in 1917. British forces in Mesopotamia went on north after Baghdad and took Mosul only after the armistice, in the middle of November 1918.Your commandMajor40 out of 100Ground held: the homeland held, with some losses; 1 place held or taken beyond the record, 2 lost or not taken18/30Power at the close: the three meters together stood at -281/20Nothing run dry: 3 meters ended at -5 or worse0/10The staff kept: 1 tr
